name: Lengthening over nail (LON)

card.summary: Hybrid limb-lengthening technique that pairs an external fixator with an intramedullary nail to shorten frame time; studied in cosmetic and non-cosmetic series.
card.note: Still a major surgery with a documented complication profile; evidence for cosmetic use comes from case series and a systematic review.

quick.overview:
Lengthening over nail combines an intramedullary nail inside the bone with an external fixator used for the lengthening phase. The nail carries the load during healing, so the frame can be removed earlier than in conventional Ilizarov lengthening.

It is one of the surgical routes discussed for cosmetic height increase, alongside fully internal motorised nails. Studies include a randomised comparison with conventional Ilizarov lengthening, a comparison with internal kinetic distraction, and case series of cosmetic lower limb lengthening.
quick.mechanism: The bone is cut and gradually distracted by the external frame while the nail is in place; after the target length is reached the frame is removed and the nail is locked, leaving the nail to stabilise the bone through consolidation.
quick.risks: Reported complications are discussed in cosmetic-lengthening reviews and individual series. One study found that reamed nailing can adversely affect bone regeneration during distraction. Pin infections, delayed healing and rehabilitation demands are described. Regulation of cosmetic lengthening varies by country.

lead: Lengthening over nail (LON) is a limb-lengthening technique in which an intramedullary nail is placed in the bone and an external fixator is used for distraction, after which the fixator is removed while the nail remains [1][3]. It was developed to minimise the time patients wear a frame during femur lengthening [1].

For height, the appeal is a permanent gain in leg length, and therefore overall stature, from surgically lengthening the femur or tibia. A systematic review of cosmetic stature lengthening reported a mean gain of 6.7 cm across 795 patients, and the Vietnamese bilateral tibial series reported an average of about 7 cm in men and 6.5 cm in women.[8][10] Compared with classic Ilizarov frames, the nail carries load during healing, so the frame can come off earlier and the bone is protected from deformity and refracture after frame removal.[6]

A prospective randomised study of 31 limbs compared LON with conventional Ilizarov lengthening on length gain, external fixation index, consolidation index and complications [3]. A 2012 study compared LON with intramedullary skeletal kinetic distraction in femoral lengthening and reported fewer complications with LON [1]. Series have reported results of cosmetic lower limb LON [9][10].
infobox: Reported in case series and a systematic review
About 1 mm per day after a latency of about a week (Wikipedia)[11]

paras: LON was developed to reduce or eliminate frame time during femur lengthening compared with conventional ring-fixator lengthening [1]. Magnetic internal lengthening nails are a related approach that avoids external devices [5]. Reference sources on distraction osteogenesis describe motorised internal nails as an alternative to external devices [11].

Wikipedia's limb-lengthening article describes distraction osteogenesis generally: a latency period of about seven days before the device is activated, distraction at roughly 1 mm per day, a consolidation phase while the bone heals, and removal of hardware in a second operation.[11] With LON the nail remains in the bone and the frame is removed earlier than in frame-only treatment.[1][6]

Wikipedia dates the first proposal of the principle to Bernhard von Langenbeck in 1869 and the first clinical series to Alessandro Codivilla in 1905, whose high complication rates meant the method was not adopted; Gavriil Ilizarov then developed external fixation and distraction rates through studies from the 1950s onward.[11] LON emerged as a hybrid of the Ilizarov frame and intramedullary nailing, intended to shorten frame time, and was compared with internal lengthening nails as those devices developed.[1][5]

In a prospective randomised study of 31 limbs in 28 patients, 15 were lengthened over a nail and 16 conventionally, and the groups were compared on fixation index, consolidation index and complications [3]. A study comparing LON with intramedullary skeletal kinetic distraction found fewer complications with LON [1]. Bilateral tibial LON has been reported with complications and psychological outcomes in a Vietnamese series [10], and results of cosmetic lower limb LON have been published [9]. A study of tibial lengthening found that reamed intramedullary nailing had an adverse effect on bone regeneration during distraction [6]. A 2020 systematic review covers cosmetic stature lengthening outcomes and complications [8]. Related studies include biological enhancement of bone healing in tibial distraction with bone marrow concentrate and platelet-rich plasma [2].

Registered studies include LON pain beliefs and functional performance after cosmetic lengthening (not yet recruiting) [12], postoperative physiotherapy after cosmetic femoral lengthening [13] and video-feedback rehabilitation after bilateral femoral lengthening [14].

A study of tibial lengthening asked whether valgus deviation increases with LON,[15] and a 2012 study of limb lengthening over plate described an alternative to nails that avoids the infection risk linked with nails.[16] A technical note on lengthening over an existing nail covers post-traumatic femoral shortening rather than cosmetic cases.[17]

A 2020 systematic review of cosmetic stature lengthening included 11 studies with 795 patients; the main techniques were classic ring Ilizarov fixators (267 patients, 33.6 percent) and LON (253 patients, 31.8 percent), with implantable lengthening nails used in 63 patients. Mean lengthening was 6.7 cm (range 1.5 to 13.0) with mean follow-up of 4.9 years, and the authors reported averages of 0.78 problems, 0.94 obstacles and 0.15 complications per patient; ankle equinus deformity was the most common problem or obstacle.[8]

A retrospective study of 32 patients with constitutional short stature (24 men, 8 women) reviewed patient selection, bone and soft-tissue complications and functional and subjective outcomes after cosmetic LON.[9] In a Vietnamese series of 104 people undergoing bilateral tibial LON with SIGN nails, tibial lengthening was about 24 percent of pre-operative tibial length in men and 21.5 percent in women; outcomes were rated excellent in 81.7 percent and good in 18.3 percent, all patients reported improved self-esteem and quality of life, and equinus contracture, pin tract infection and valgus deviation were the most common complications.[10]

Reference sources note that cosmetic stature lengthening is unregulated in some countries, that infection, additional surgeries and shorter-than-expected gains have been reported, and that China's health ministry banned limb lengthening in 2006 after serious side effects [11].

Wikipedia reports that in India cosmetic lengthening is unregulated, that people as young as 13 or 14 have had the procedure, and that some patients developed infections and needed further surgery to walk or gained less height than expected.[11] Equinus contracture, pin tract infection and valgus deviation are the complications most often named in LON series, and a study of tibial lengthening reported that reamed nailing can adversely affect bone regeneration during distraction.[6][10]

timeline.event: Bernhard von Langenbeck proposes surgical bone lengthening (per Wikipedia).[11]
Alessandro Codivilla publishes the first clinical series, with high complication rates.[11]
China's health ministry bans limb lengthening after serious side effects.[11]
Study reports fewer complications with LON than intramedullary skeletal kinetic distraction [1].
Randomised comparison of LON and conventional Ilizarov lengthening published [3].
Systematic review of cosmetic stature lengthening published [8].
Vietnamese series of 104 bilateral tibial LON patients published.[10]

chain: Bone is cut and gradually distracted by an external frame over a nail
New bone forms in the gap while the nail holds alignment
Permanent added leg length and taller standing height
angle.text: LON lengthens the femur or tibia surgically, with studies of cosmetic patients reporting average gains of roughly 6 to 7 cm. The nail shortens the time the external frame is worn compared with conventional frame-only methods.
